newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek C/A deficit jumps to $456 mln in June.
newsitem.headline: Greek C/A deficit jumps to $456 mln in June.

text.p: Greece's current account deficit rose provisionally to $456 million in June from $152.8 million in the same month a year ago, the Bank of Greece said.
The wider deficit was caused exclusively by a 30 percent drop in the surplus of invisibles mainly because of a severe drop in foreign exchange revenues from tourism, it said.
The January-June cumulative current account deficit widened to $3.155 billion from $2.141 billion in the same period in 1995, a rise of 47.3 percent, it said.
The trade deficit fell 5.8 percent year-on-year in June to $1.37 billion from $1.454 billion in June 1995.
The cumulative trade deficit was up 3.8 percent to $8.9 billion in the first half compared to $8.6 billion in the same period in 1995.

Foreign exchange reserves stood at $13 billion in June from $16.5 billion in the same month a year ago but rose again to $16.8 billion at the end of September, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
